---
title: "To req(), the number 0 is a valid value"
ref: SHY-04
categories: [Shiny]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'shiny::isTruthy(0)'
reponse: 'TRUE'
attendu: "`FALSE`, like `FALSE`, `NULL` or `\"\"`"
versions: "All versions of {shiny}"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2020)"
---

::: {.piege packages="shiny"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shiny))

isTruthy(0)
isTruthy(FALSE)
isTruthy("")
req(0)
```
:::

## Why

`req()` silently stops a reactive computation when a value is not "truthy". The list is short: `FALSE`, `NULL`, `""`, an empty vector, a vector made only of `NA`, a `try()` error, and an action button that was never clicked.

The number 0 is not on it. A `numericInput()` left at 0 therefore gets through `req()`, and the computation runs with a zero quantity. Only the action button is an exception: its value 0 carries a special class that `isTruthy()` recognises.

## The remedy

Give `req()` the business rule itself, as a logical test.

::: {.piege packages="shiny"}
```{r}
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shiny))

quantity <- 0
isTruthy(quantity > 0)
tryCatch(req(quantity > 0), error = function(e) {
  class(e)[1]
})
```
:::
